chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi narrated to me. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Ya'fur narrated to me from Musa ibn Abi Ayyub al-Tamimi from Musa ibn al-Mughira from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim.

He said: Ali (peace be upon him) was mentioned in the presence of Ibn Abbas after his death, so he said: 'How tragic is the loss of Abu al-Hasan! He passed away, by God — he never changed, never substituted, never fell short, never hoarded, never withheld, and never preferred anything except God. By God, this world was more trivial to him than the sole of his sandal. A lion in battle, an ocean in gatherings, a sage among sages. Alas, he has passed on to the exalted ranks.'

key_terms.بَحْرٌ فِي الْمَجَالِسِ: An ocean in gatherings; epithet for one of boundless knowledge and generosity
key_terms.شِسْعِ نَعْلِهِ: The sole or strap of his sandal; a proverbial expression for something utterly worthless
key_terms.لَيْثٌ فِي الْوَغَى: A lion in battle; classical epithet for an outstanding warrior
key_terms.وَا أَسَفَاهُ: Exclamation of profound grief; classical Arabic lament formula

ai.seo_question: What did Ibn Abbas say about Imam Ali after his death?
ai.summary: This hadith preserves Ibn Abbas's moving eulogy of Imam Ali (AS) after his martyrdom in 40 AH. Ibn Abbas, the Prophet's cousin and one of the most learned companions, testifies to Ali's uncompromising integrity, asceticism, and multifaceted excellence. The original audience — early Muslims who knew both men personally — would have understood this as the highest possible testimony from a man famed for his scholarship and proximity to the Prophet's household, validating Ali's singular status among the companions.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Jarir al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan b. Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. `Abd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi narrated to me. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Ya`fur narrated to me from Musa b. Abi Ayyub al-Tamimi from Musa b. al-Mughira from al-Dahhak b. Mazahim.

He said: `Ali (as) was mentioned in the presence of Ibn `Abbas after his death, so he said: How tragic is what happened to Abi’l Hasan! He passed away, and by Allah, he did not change anything, nor did he exchange anything, nor did he shorten anything, nor did he join anything, nor did he prevent anything, nor did he affect anything except for the sake of Allah. By Allah, this world was less significant to him than the sole of his sandal. He was a lion in battle, an ocean in gatherings, and a sage among the sages. Alas, he has passed onto the exalted ranks.
